title: Coefficient comparison for ordinary direct image
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $f\colon X\to Y$ is a $k$-morphism. The listed coefficient maps mean homomorphisms $A\to B$ of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$; $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ and $E\to F$ for finite extensions $F/E$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; $\mathcal O_E\to E$; $E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; continuous homomorphisms $\mathcal O_E\to A$ to finite rings killed by powers of $\ell$; and finite composites of these maps. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ is its valuation ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]; the topological rings are regarded as condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with the filtered-colimit condensed convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Write $K_{\Lambda'}=\Lambda'_X\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}K$ for the derived coefficient change [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], and $\Dctf$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Use the derived module adjunctions of [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction].

For such a listed coefficient map $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ and $K\in\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ let
$$
\gamma_{f,K}\colon(Rf_*K)_{\Lambda'}\longrightarrow Rf_*f^*\bigl((Rf_*K)_{\Lambda'}\bigr)\simeq Rf_*\bigl((f^*Rf_*K)_{\Lambda'}\bigr)\xrightarrow{Rf_*((\epsilon_K)_{\Lambda'})}Rf_*(K_{\Lambda'})
$$
be the composite of the unit of $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ on $\D(-_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda')$, the
pullback identification of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), and the extension of
scalars of the counit $\epsilon_K\colon f^*Rf_*K\to K$. Then:

1. $\gamma_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism for $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$; both sides lie in
   $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$.
2. $\gamma$ is natural in $K$, compatible with composition
   ($\gamma_{gf,K}=Rg_*(\gamma_{f,K})\circ\gamma_{g,Rf_*K}$ under $R(gf)_*=Rg_*Rf_*$), and
   compatible with the units and counits of $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ over $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$:
   writing $T_Z=(-)_{\Lambda'}$ and $c_f\colon f_{\Lambda'}^*T_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Xf_\Lambda^*$ for the inverse of the pullback identification, the unit and counit equations are
   $$\gamma_{f,f_\Lambda^*N}\circ T_Y(\eta_N)=Rf_{*,\Lambda'}(c_{f,N})\circ\eta'_{T_YN},$$
   $$\epsilon'_{T_XK}\circ f_{\Lambda'}^*(\gamma_{f,K})=T_X(\epsilon_K)\circ c_{f,Rf_{*,\Lambda}K}.$$
   These identities hold on the ambient derived categories wherever the displayed objects are defined.

proof.text:
Put $T_Z=(-)_{\Lambda'}$, $L=f_\Lambda^*$, $R=Rf_{*,\Lambda}$, $L'=f_{\Lambda'}^*$, $R'=Rf_{*,\Lambda'}$, and let $c_f:L'T_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_XL$ be the inverse of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1). The adjunctions exist by [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], and [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies underived module pullback canonically with the exact lift of inverse image: its underlying sheaf functor is $f^{-1}$ and its coefficient action is transported using $\alpha_f^{-1}$. We use this natural identification, with its transported action, whenever identifying module pullback with inverse image below. The component formula in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives precisely
$\gamma_K=R'(T_X\epsilon_K)\,R'(c_{f,RK})\,\eta'_{T_YRK}$.
Thus $\gamma$ is a natural transformation. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) to the pullback squares for $g$ and $f$, using the composition compatibility in [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1): its mate is $Rg_{*,\Lambda'}(\gamma_{f,K})\circ\gamma_{g,Rf_{*,\Lambda}K}$. Apply part (1) of the same pasting lemma to successive coefficient changes, and [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](3): for $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$ one gets $\gamma^{\Lambda\to\Lambda''}_{f,K}=\gamma^{\Lambda'\to\Lambda''}_{f,T_XK}\circ T_Y^{\Lambda'\to\Lambda''}(\gamma^{\Lambda\to\Lambda'}_{f,K})$, with the tensor reassociations. No assertion that an arbitrary mate of an isomorphism is invertible is used.

source.place: Formal properties: definition, naturality, and the two pasting laws

proof.text: The counit equation is exactly the transpose description in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For the unit equation, transpose $\gamma_{LN}T_Y\eta_N$ under $L'\dashv R'$. Its transpose is $T_X\epsilon_{LN}\,c_{f,RLN}\,L'T_Y\eta_N$. By naturality of $c_f$ this equals $T_X(\epsilon_{LN}L\eta_N)c_{f,N}=c_{f,N}$, using the triangle identity for $L\dashv R$. The transpose of $R'c_{f,N}\,\eta'_{T_YN}$ is also $c_{f,N}$ by the other triangle identity. The bijection of mates proves the unit equation. This proves all the requested adjunction compatibility, without assuming that $\gamma$ is already invertible.

source.place: Formal properties: explicit unit and counit equations

proof.text: Restriction of scalars must be handled at the derived level. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with $R_Z=\Lambda_Z$, $S_Z=\Lambda'_Z$ and the Cartesian identifications of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. The commuting ring square is part of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. This gives the canonical restriction/direct-image isomorphism and says that restriction reflects isomorphisms and respects transposes, with no flatness assumption on $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$. Consequently, after restricting $\gamma$ to $\Lambda$, it is the projection morphism for the coefficient complex $\Lambda'_Y$: both have transpose $f^*(\Lambda'_Y\otimes^L Rf_*K)\simeq\Lambda'_X\otimes^L f^*Rf_*K\to\Lambda'_X\otimes^L K$. The tensor comparison and this exact projection morphism are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. It is therefore enough below to prove that the underlying projection morphism is invertible.

source.place: Formal properties: restriction of scalars and normalization of the projection map

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target], applied to $X\to Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $X$ is finite type and $Y$ is separated over $k$ by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Its diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal $X\to X\times_kX$ along $X\times_YX\to X\times_kX$; the identification of this pullback with $X$ follows directly from the fibre-product universal property. Hence $f$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and the definition in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. In particular it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images](3) applies to $f$ at both coefficient stages. For $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, its pushforward lies in $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, so [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf](3) puts the source of $\gamma$ in $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$. The same coefficient-change assertion first on $X$, followed by the direct-image assertion over $\Lambda'$, puts its target there too. The coefficient pasting law in step 1 now reduces invertibility for finite composites to invertibility for each elementary listed map; the intermediate complexes stay in $\Dctf$ by [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf](3).

source.place: Preservation and reduction to elementary coefficient maps

proof.text:
For a finite admissible ring $A$, the discrete condensed ring on the point is the sheafification of the constant ring $A$: a continuous function $S	o A$ is locally constant and is therefore constant on a finite clopen partition. The inverse image $p_Z^*$ preserves colimits and finite limits, so it takes this constant ring to the constant ring on $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$; compare [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. In particular these are precisely the finite coefficients to which [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] applies. (A finite ring is Noetherian because every ideal is generated by its finite underlying set.) That node supplies $K'\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ and $
u_X^*K'\simeq K$. Define the étale derived extension $K'_B$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. After restriction to $A$, its K-flat model is the derived $A$-tensor with $B_X$. For $B$ finite, $K'_B$ is bounded: its underlying $A$-complex has cohomology in the Tor interval of $K'$. The comparison $
u^*$ commutes with this derived tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the comparison morphism with $
u^{-1}A=A$, $
u^{-1}B=B$. For $f$ qcqs, [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] identifies the two direct images of these bounded-below complexes, compatibly with units and counits. Write $ eta_{f,L}^A:
u_Y^*Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{ét}}L\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{proét}}
u_X^*L$ for this comparison, and define $ eta^B$ likewise. Under $K\simeq
u_X^*K'$, the pro-étale coefficient map is the composite
$$(Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{proét}}
u_X^*K')_B
\xrightarrow{( eta^A_{f,K'})^{-1}_B}(
u_Y^*Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{ét}}K')_B
\simeq
u_Y^*((Rf_{*,A}^{\mathrm{ét}}K')_B)
\xrightarrow{
u_Y^*\gamma^{\mathrm{ét}}}
u_Y^*Rf_{*,B}^{\mathrm{ét}}K'_B
\xrightarrow{ eta^B_{f,K'_B}}Rf_{*,B}^{\mathrm{proét}}
u_X^*K'_B.$$
Indeed, take its $B$-coefficient pro-étale $f$-transpose. The counit compatibility of $ eta^B$ replaces the last arrow followed by the pro-étale counit by the pullback of the étale counit. The defining transpose of $\gamma^{\mathrm{ét}}$ then gives the $B$-extension of $
u_X^*\epsilon^A_{K'}$. The counit compatibility of $ eta^A$, together with its inverse in the first arrow, identifies this with the $B$-extension of the pro-étale counit. This is precisely the defining transpose of $\gamma^{\mathrm{proét}}$, so the adjunction bijection proves equality. Thus invertibility of the étale map proves the pro-étale case.

source.place: Finite rings: passage to the classical étale category

proof.text:
Use the relative, rather than absolute, cohomological dimension. By [lem-kun-0f10](1), $\operatorname{cd}(f)<\infty$ for the $k$-morphism $f$ between finite-type $k$-schemes. By [def-kun-cd] this bounds all torsion abelian higher direct images by one integer $N$. Every $A$-module sheaf is killed by a power of $\ell$, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison] identifies its higher direct images after forgetting coefficients with the abelian ones. Thus the bound required by [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] holds for all $A$-module sheaves. The finite $A$-module $B$ is finitely presented by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation], and $K'$ is bounded, hence in $D^-$. Apply [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] with $M=B$: the underlying $A$-projection $Rf_*K'\otimes_A^L B_Y\to Rf_*(K'\otimes_A^L B_X)$ is invertible. To identify the actual $B$-linear map, let $Q=(Rf_{*,A}K')_B$. The underlying $A$-complex of $Q$ is the left side of the projection isomorphism just proved; its right side is $Rf_{*,A}$ of the bounded complex underlying $K'_B$. Hence $Q$ is bounded below. Thus both $Q$ and $K'_B$ meet the bounded-below hypotheses of [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons] and [lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-derived-adjunction-identities]. Use their canonical restriction/direct-image isomorphism to identify the restriction of the target with $Rf_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}(K'_B)$. The stated unit and counit identities show that the $A$-adjunct of the restricted $B$-coefficient $\gamma$ is
$$f_A^*\bigl(Rf_{*,A}K'\otimes_A^LB_Y\bigr)\simeq f_A^*Rf_{*,A}K'\otimes_A^LB_X\xrightarrow{\epsilon^A_{K'}\otimes1}K'\otimes_A^LB_X.$$
This is the defining adjunct of the projection map supplied by [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant], so the two maps agree by the adjunction bijection. Restriction is exact and conservative because it leaves underlying sheaves unchanged ([lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]); in particular it detects isomorphisms on cohomology. No faithfulness of restriction on derived morphisms is needed. Therefore the étale comparison, and hence the pro-étale comparison in step 5, is invertible. This works even when $B$ has infinite projective dimension over $A$.

source.place: Finite rings: relative cohomological-dimension projection argument; repair of the absolute-dimension inference

proof.text: For a bounded complex $F$ of finite free condensed $\Lambda$-modules, put $F_Z=p_Z^*F$. The monoidal natural isomorphism of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp] identifies $f^*F_Y$ with $F_X$: its compatibility with the action map $\Lambda\otimes F\to F$ makes it module-linear, and naturality makes it commute with the differentials. Apply the exact natural projection transformation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] to the second variable $F_Y$. It is the identity for $F=\Lambda$, hence an isomorphism for every finite direct sum of shifts of $\Lambda$. Its compatibility with triangles, including connecting maps, is explicitly part of the cited node. Build $F$ by the successive brutal truncation triangles, adding its single finite-free terms one at a time. Induction on the number of nonzero terms and [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] prove the projection is an isomorphism for $F$. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](2), for $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ and $E\to F$, the second coefficient sheaf is finite free over the first on every scheme. For these two maps, apply the same projection transformation directly to $P=\Lambda'_Y$ in degree zero. Choose a finite-free basis on $Y$, so $P\simeq\Lambda_Y^{\oplus r}$; pull back this basis to identify $f^*P\simeq\Lambda'_X$ using [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1). Naturality with the $r$ summand inclusions identifies its projection map with $r$ copies of the unit-coefficient identity. It is therefore invertible, and step 3 proves these cases of $\gamma$. This uses finite freeness of the coefficient sheaf on $Y$, exactly as stated in the cited node.

source.place: Finite free and finite-complex coefficient extensions

proof.text: For a listed continuous $\mathcal O_E\to A$ with $A$ finite, put $O=\mathcal O_E$. Continuity and discreteness imply $\pi_E^n A=0$ for some $n\ge1$. The ring $O$ is a DVR, in particular a PID, by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Choose finitely many generators of the finite $O$-module $A$ and a surjection $O^r\to A$. Its kernel $P$ is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] and is torsion-free as a submodule of $O^r$, so [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] makes it finite free. Thus $0\to O^s\xrightarrow{\phi}O^r\to A\to0$ is a finite free resolution. Since $\pi_E^nO^r\subseteq P$, its inclusion becomes an isomorphism after passing to $E$, so $s=r$ and the matrix $\phi$ is invertible over $E$. Its inverse matrix over $E$ is continuous, so the bijection $O^r\to P$ is a homeomorphism onto its image with the induced topology. For every profinite $S$, a continuous map $S\to A$ lifts to $O^r$ by choosing one lift for each of its finitely many values; a continuous map to the kernel lifts through $\phi$ by the continuous inverse just described. Using [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], this proves exactness of the sequence of condensed modules, including at its left term. Pulling it back by $p_Z^*$ preserves exactness by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] and finite free terms by [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. The resulting two-term complex of finite free $O_Z$-modules in degrees $-1,0$ resolves $A_Z$; its only nonzero terms are in degrees $-1,0$ and are flat, so [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes it K-flat. The source of this precise criterion is Stacks Tag 06YQ, label lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat in sites-cohomology.tex; Tag 06YS is the distinct existence theorem for K-flat resolutions. Thus this two-term resolution computes tensoring with $A_Z$ even when $K$ is not flat. Apply step 7 to this two-term complex and step 3 to detect invertibility after restriction. This proves $O\to A$. For the zero ring $A$, take the zero module and both sides are zero.

source.place: Finite presented coefficient extension: the two-term condensed free resolution; its K-flatness uses Stacks sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 06YQ, label lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (not Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution).

proof.text: We record explicitly the colimit calculation used for the last two coefficient maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], module colimits and their underlying sheaf colimits agree. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact], filtered colimits of these modules are exact. If $S_Z=\varinjlim_i P_{i,Z}$ with each $P_{i,Z}$ finite free over $R_Z$, then $S_Z\otimes_{R_Z}M=\varinjlim_i(P_{i,Z}\otimes_{R_Z}M)$ by the balanced-coequalizer construction in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]: an $R_Z$-balanced bilinear map out of $(\varinjlim_iP_{i,Z})\times M$ is exactly a compatible family of balanced bilinear maps out of $P_{i,Z}\times M$. The tensor universal property therefore gives the displayed isomorphism, with each colimit coprojection corresponding to its tensor with $M$. Each functor on the right is exact, so their filtered colimit is exact: $S_Z$ is flat. Consequently ordinary termwise tensor with $S_Z$ sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and computes derived scalar extension, by its K-flat definition [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. It also commutes with cohomology, as does the termwise filtered colimit. To apply bounded continuity, choose a representative $C$ of $K$ and a degree $a$ below its cohomology; replace it by the good lower truncation, with $\operatorname{coker}(d^{a-1})$ in degree $a$ and zero below $a$. The map to this truncation is a quasi-isomorphism because its cohomology agrees in every degree. Tensoring its terms with each flat $P_{i,X}$ gives complexes zero below the same $a$. Thus every colimit diagram below meets the literal common lower bound required by [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image].

source.place: Bounded representatives, exact filtered colimits, and flatness for the two localization cases

proof.text:
For $O=\mathcal O_E\to E$, [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] identifies $E_Z$ with the sequential colimit $O_Z\xrightarrow{\ell}O_Z\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots$, compatibly with pullback. Each term is rank-one free, so step 9 applies and $K_E$ is represented by $\varinjlim(C\xrightarrow{\ell}C\to\cdots)$ with a common lower bound. Since $f$ is qcqs, [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image] gives
$H^q(Rf_*(K_E))\simeq\varinjlim(H^q(Rf_*K)\xrightarrow{\ell}H^q(Rf_*K)\to\cdots)$.
Flatness and exactness from step 9 identify this last sheaf with $H^q((Rf_*K)_E)$. This is the map induced by $\gamma$, not merely an abstract isomorphism: the $i$th colimit coprojection $O_Y\to E_Y$ is the $O_Y$-linear map $x\mapsto\ell^{-i}x$ (with initial index $0$), and need not be a ring homomorphism, and naturality of the projection transformation [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] makes $\gamma$ compose with it as $Rf_*$ of the corresponding coprojection on $X$. Therefore the continuity isomorphism is $H^q(\gamma)$ for every $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] and the conservative restriction in step 3, $\gamma$ is invertible.

source.place: Localization $\mathcal O_E\to E$: canonical map on every cohomology sheaf

proof.text:
For $E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] presents the target coefficient sheaf as the filtered colimit of the $F_Z$ for finite extensions $F/E$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Restricting its original index of all finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ to those containing $E$ is cofinal: any finite extension is contained in its compositum with $E$, still finite. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](2), each $F_Z$ is finite free over $E_Z$. Use the representative $C$ of step 9, zero below the fixed degree $a$; $C_F$ is termwise a finite sum of $C$, so the complexes $C_F$ have a common lower bound. The case $E\to F$ in step 7 and [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image] give
$H^q((Rf_*K)_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell})\simeq\varinjlim_F H^q((Rf_*K)_F)\xrightarrow{\varinjlim H^q(\gamma_F)}\varinjlim_FH^q(Rf_*K_F)\simeq H^q(Rf_*(K_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}))$.
The middle maps are isomorphisms. For an inclusion $F\subseteq G$, the square of these maps commutes by naturality of the projection transformation in its coefficient complex [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. For the maps $F_Z\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Z}$ the same naturality identifies the displayed colimit map with $H^q(\gamma)$. The cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] and step 3 prove this last case. Together with step 4 and the formal properties of steps 1–2, this finishes both clauses.

source_error.failed_inference: Finite type over the arbitrary standing field does not imply finite absolute ell-cohomological dimension.
